analysis.file_name: ConocoPhillips (COP)_ To Divest North Sea Business Segment.pdf
analysis.title: ConocoPhillips (COP): To Divest North Sea Business Segment; Focus Cores Up to Alaska, Permian, Canada and LNG
key_insights: COP announced a definitive agreement on 11/23 to sell its Norway business and a 40.25% interest in and operatorship of the UK Teesside oil terminal to Vår Energi for $4.425bn headline value.
Net cash proceeds are $2.5bn after roughly $0.5bn of adjustments as of January 1, 2026. Adjusted consideration of $3.9bn also includes about $1.4bn of remaining 2026 tax liability payable in 1H27.
The deal monetizes roughly 120,000 BOE/d of 2025 production and about 221 MMBOE of year-end 2025 proved reserves, and transfers decommissioning liabilities to the buyer.
Assets include the operated Greater Ekofisk Area, eight partner-operated fields, the Norpipe oil pipeline interest and Teesside terminal infrastructure.
Close is expected by end of 1Q27, subject to approval by the Norwegian Ministry of Energy and other regulatory conditions.
GS expects proceeds to go to general purposes and discretionary buybacks next year, which would be upside to the baseline commitment to return 45% of cash from operations.
Capital is to be reallocated to higher-return, lower cost-of-supply projects across the global portfolio.
GS keeps a Buy rating and $156 12-month price target on COP, with 14.6% upside from $136.12.

market_movers.rationale: Norway and Teesside divestiture streamlines the portfolio and may fund discretionary buybacks above the 45% CFO return baseline.

earnings_insights: GS estimates COP EPS of $12.07 for 12/26E, $11.07 for 12/27E and $10.56 for 12/28E, versus $6.17 for 12/25 (basis not specified in the report).
GS quarterly EPS estimates: $3.68 for 12/26E, $2.76 for 3/27E and $2.65 for 6/27E, versus $3.28 for 9/26 (basis not specified).
risk_factors: Transaction closing depends on Norwegian Ministry of Energy approval and other regulatory conditions.
